findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed grease and dust debris on hood baffles above fryers. Informed PIC that hood needs to be cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of grease and dust. Ensure the hood system is clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the seal on the back hand sink to be cracked and damaged. Ensure sealant is replaced before next routine inspection to prevent moisture and bacterial growth.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no Certified Food Protection Manager in kitchen during time of inspection. PIC reported that the CFPM is on break. Ensure that a CFPM is present at all times of food service/preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food items to measure above the maximum cold holding temperature for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods:
1. Cut tomato
2. Cut lettuce
3. Sour cream
4. Mayonnaise
5. Spicy mayonnaise

The cut tomato was measured with a probe thermometer, and measured 48F. The items on the above list were voluntarily discarded. The consumer-style refrigerator will now only be used for non-TCS foods. The newer commercial cooler will hold all TCS foods moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the following ready-to-eat TCS foods to be missing proper date marking:
1. Cooked spaghetti in sauce
2. Cooked chicken
3. Sour cream
4. Cottage cheese
5. Milk

Ensure that all ready-to-eat TCS foods are date marked if stored longer than 24 hours after opening. These items need to be discarded 7 days following opening/preparation. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/31/2025 to ensure date marking compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed food containers (aluminum pans and paper boats) stored without adequate coverings to avoid cross contamination. Ensure food containers are either covered or inverted to protect food-contact surface.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed grease and dust debris on hood baffles above fryers. Informed PIC that hood needs to be cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of grease and dust.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the kitchen flooring to be excessively sticky and soiled. Ensure flooring in the food prep areas are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed employee phone, purse, and other personal items stored on food contact and non-food contact surfaces in the kitchen. There is a shelf dedicated for personal items. Ensure the designated shelf is free of food items for sale, and there are no food items below the shelf. Ensure all personal items are stored in designated areas to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed no CFPM on site with allergen certification. Ensure there is a CFPM on site at all times with valid allergen certification to properly educate consumers on risk of allergen exposure.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed container of cooked chicken wings in cooler to have no date mark. Per PIC, chicken wings were cooked today. Item was properly date marked during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed bare wooden pallet under stove in kitchen. Seal bare wood pallet, or remove it from kitchen. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop head stored head down in mop bucket. Store wet mop head in a fashion that promotes quick drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee fail to use barrier to turn off faucet after washing hands. Use a barrier (paper towel) to turn off faucet after hand washing. Discussed proper hand washing technique with employee. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available for use at front area hand sink. Paper towels were provided during inspection. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed individual containers of macaroni and cheese in kitchen cooler to not have a date mark. Per PIC, items were prepared the day before inspection. Items were marked with proper date during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed to-go containers in front area to be stored with food contact surface exposed. Store to-go containers in an inverted fashion to protect against contamination. To-go containers were place in an inverted fashion during inspection. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed certified food manager on duty to not have additional allergen training certification. All certified food managers at facility must have additional allergen training certification. Provide facility with additional allergen training handout. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
